about: build.optimizer_patches rule `no-ctor-evaluation`: GlobalOpt without static-constructor evaluation. Stock
GlobalOpt hands a unit's static initializers (llvm.global_ctors, such as _GLOBAL__sub_I_*) to
llvm::optimizeGlobalCtorsList (llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils/CtorUtils.cpp), which runs them at compile time and,
when it can, folds what they store into the globals' initializers and drops the code. A toolchain whose
optimizer did not evaluate them keeps every static initializer as code that stores at startup. No option turns
the evaluation off, so the rule is a byte patch: optimizeGlobalCtorsList returns false (nothing changed) before
it reads llvm.global_ctors. It changes the optimizer (build.optimizer), not the code generator. zkit applies a
patch to a copy of the official binary whose SHA-256 is the patch's `sha256`, checks each edit's `old` bytes
first and the result against `patched_sha256` (build.patched_clang). Offsets are file offsets; each `why` names

patches.release: LLVM 19.1.7 for Linux x86-64, LLVM-19.1.7-Linux-X64.tar.xz: bin/clang-19 (bin/clang and bin/clang++ link to it)

edits.why: 0x69ed810 push rbp; push r15 -> xor eax, eax; ret: the function returns false before it reads llvm.global_ctors
